master: One single production animation source sprite for Bullets of Fury, a FIRE WHIP made of roaring orange-red fire, no ship and no handle. Use the fire texture and tapering needle tip of the reference, but show ONLY ONE complete curved whip, not a sheet. Square transparent canvas 256x256. Fixed emission ROOT at pixel (128,220). Length about 100 pixels. Whip arcs LEFT and UP, ends near (35,165), with a loose flowing curl and razor-fine tapered flame tip. Leave room above and to the right for a later wide left-to-right lash animation. Shape must read as a slender flexible burning lash, not a cone/flamethrower or lightning bolt. Body about 8 pixels thick with thin flickering tongues; root about 12 pixels, progressively thinner toward tip. 16-bit arcade hand-shaded pixel fire: deep crimson shadows, saturated red and fiery orange mids, golden amber core, no white/pink core, no blue. Keep crisp detailed pixel clusters. Exact root position, no muzzle ring, no extra pieces, no smoke, no text, no duplicated whips.
animation: Animate this ONE curved fire whip through a complete seamless LEFT to RIGHT to LEFT lash cycle. The thick emitting root at its bottom stays absolutely fixed as if attached to the nose of a stationary player ship; do not draw any ship. Begin with the thin pointed tip extended far left, draw it back into a loose curl, cast the root toward the right with the flexible middle following, then the tip snaps outward to the far right. Reverse naturally: the root leads back left, a travelling S-bend runs down the lash, the pointed tip lags and cracks to the far left, reconnecting to the first pose. Whip remains about the same length and weight, with a narrow tapered tip, never becomes a ball or explosion. Fire tongues flicker rapidly along the whole lash throughout. Keep root position fixed, camera fixed, consistent scale and transparent background. Give the tip room on BOTH sides: motion spans a broad semicircle above the root. No spinning around its center, no screen translation, no fades, no generated muzzle ring. The full whip silhouette must change naturally in every frame, with clear curling anticipation and a sharp uncoiling follow-through.
